Capability.meaning: Explicit operation grant on a resource or permission scope.

PrincipalGroup.meaning: Direct membership in a configured role or user group; a group can itself be a member. Supplied by trusted configuration or an authoritative identity source, never inferred from an agent-chosen name.

ResourceGroup.meaning: Permission-scope membership; grants on a parent apply to its descendants.

InGroup.meaning: Direct or nested role/user-group membership from PrincipalGroup. Membership alone is not permission.

Can.meaning: Grant including declared principal and resource memberships; not final authorization.

Field.meaning: Host-observed field or association of an application object or event. The binding defines cardinality, value type, fixed unit and optional observation-time field; never agent claims or hidden policy decisions.

Event.meaning: An event observed by the host, with its ID, actor and kind; recording it does not imply permission or success.

scope: Captured gate inputs and mediated callbacks. Outcomes follow the trusted adapter's confirmation contract; they are not independent proof of business success or authentic identity. Unmediated channels and missing observations remain outside this trace.

The 2,162% cumulative TSR under Cook is attributed to the proxy, which is a governance filing rather than a performance record.

Microsoft appears in no competitor row although it leads every multiple table, is the only other closed hardware-plus-OS-plus-subscription ecosystem and is shipping Copilot+ on ARM against the Mac. Meta appears only as \"Meta in glasses\" although it leads the glasses segment the section says grows 18.1% a year and recruited Apple's AI staff (S121). No named assistant substitute (ChatGPT, Gemini app, Copilot) is mapped against Siri, though the section's own threat list is \"AI agents that could move the assistant layer off the operating system\". parameters.notes: Checklist run against the lens. Geographic: Greater China, Japan, Europe and Rest of Asia-Pacific are covered with dated share; India is treated as a supply base and a demand market, but Indian and Emerging Asia vendors (Transsion, Lava, Micromax) do not appear as price-tier competitors. Adjacent giants: Microsoft (PC, Copilot, Azure AI), Amazon (Alexa, cloud, no device overlap) and Meta (glasses, AI talent) are the three that could enter with existing infrastructure; only Alphabet and Samsung are mapped. Substitutes: the status quo row (longer device life) is present and well evidenced; an assistant bought outside the OS is described but not named. Open source: no relevance to consumer hardware except on-device model licensing, which the report covers through the Gemini deal. Academic spin-outs: none material. Supplier-as-competitor: Samsung and SK hynix supply the memory whose 146% price rise compresses Apple's margin while Samsung competes in handsets - a vertical conflict the section does not draw out.

Substitutes: the status quo row (longer device life) is present and well evidenced; an assistant bought outside the OS is described but not named. Open source: no relevance to consumer hardware except on-device model licensing, which the report covers through the Gemini deal. Academic spin-outs: none material. Supplier-as-competitor: Samsung and SK hynix supply the memory whose 146% price rise compresses Apple's margin while Samsung competes in handsets - a vertical conflict the section does not draw out.

parameters.notes: PMF questions and where the report stands. Who is the budget owner: consumer or carrier financing for hardware (terms not given), developer and subscriber for services (well argued, with the 76.3% margin and the 2.1x R&D cover). Sales cycle: the annual September launch is described and the two-cycle year is a real insight; the enterprise and education channel is not examined. Why not faster: answered well for AI - 23 months from Apple Intelligence to a beta, a licensed model, the December 2025 reorganisation - and not at all for price. Lost deals: never addressed; candidates are the AI researchers lost to Meta, the ~60% collapse of the sub-$100 segment, and the lost default-assistant position on rival platforms. The one adoption claim that would settle the AI cycle is missing: no iOS 27 share, no assistant usage, no iPhone 18 mix. Durability of the $2,550 foldable is flagged as a milestone but with no evidence behind the 17M-unit forecast.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Give each scenario its own EPS built from its stated margin and services assumptions, add a joint case (gross margin 44/46/48% against the search payment intact, lower or banned) with value per share, and restate the probability-weighted value and the tranche logic from that table.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The scenario table varies only the exit multiple. Bull, base and bear all carry the same FY2027 EPS ($10.20 or $9.79) and differ by 35x/29x/24.6x, while their narratives specify different margins and services outcomes. On the report's own sensitivity (200bp of gross margin = $0.52 of EPS) the bear's \"hardware margin below 46%\" gives EPS near $9.3 and 24.6x, or $229, not $241 - which puts the weighted value near $288.5, not $291.5 - and the joint case that risk describes (46% margin plus a cut payment) is never computed.","sections":["thesis","risk","scoring"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Recompute on market value at each entry price and restate; the point that each leg down raises forward EPS growth survives at 2.2-2.4%, not 3.0-3.6%.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The buyback retention figures are wrong by about a third: \"the same $82-85bn a year retires 3.0% of the shares at $270 and 3.6% at $240, against 1.7% at today's price\". At $270 the market value is about $3,941bn, so $85bn is 2.2%; at $240, about $3,503bn, so 2.4%. The 1.7% base is right ($85bn / $5,029.6bn = 1.69%), which makes the other two impossible on the same method.","sections":["exit"],"severity":"Important"}]
parameters.notes: Arithmetic checked and sound: 200bp of gross margin = $466.8bn x 2% x 0.827 / 14.715bn shares = $0.52, or 6.0% of $8.72; the $20bn payment is 15.0% of FY2025 operating income and 12.8% of net income; incremental operating margin 43.0%; composite score 6.05 from the weighted table; probability-weighted return -15.4% at $344.63 and +7.8% at $270; the exit grid's three-year IRRs (1.3%, 4.5%, -3.2%) all reproduce from FY2029 EPS of $11.45 plus $3.55 of dividends. Stress test of the 30%-worse case: a 30% gross-margin cut is not the exposure - 46% is the report's own bear and it costs 5-6% of value at the proposed entry; a 30% revenue fall at the 43% incremental margin gives EPS near $5.4 and $95bn of operating income, which the $62.2bn net cash absorbs, so the thesis survives 30% worse on the business and fails only on the multiple. Two numbers I could not rebuild and would not charge: the 320.6% ROIC (its inputs are not shown, and the section already calls it an artefact) and the 2,162% cumulative TSR under Cook, attributed to the proxy.
